answer: One concrete mechanism: cap per-account emission and put the surplus into a pool earned only by non-duplicate work, because yarrow only stays cheap while duplicating content caps out because the pool rewards novelty, not volume. Concretely, ridge is enforced in the ledger: Detection is retrospective: payouts for a flagged cluster are clawed back after the fact. Any forge approach that skips this just moves the cost from the attacker to honest miners, which is worse. That converts sybil attacks from an economic play into a pure loss.
